news.headline: Perimeter Debuts At Intermountain Health With FDA-Approved AI System For Breast Cancer Surgery
news.summary: Industry trade press picked up Perimeter's first commercial deployment, framing Claire as the first PMA-approved, AI-enabled intraoperative margin assessment system to move from clinical trials into routine surgical practice. The coverage carried the story into the week of the Q2 report and kept the shares elevated.

news.headline: Intermountain Health Deploys Claire OCT System to Aid Breast Cancer Surgery
news.summary: Follow-up coverage added the first operating-room feedback, with Intermountain breast surgeon Dr. Teresa Reading saying Claire folded easily into her workflow and that the AI quickly directed her attention to areas of concern. Workflow fit is the key adoption question for a device that has to run inside a live lumpectomy.

news.headline: Intermountain Health Brings Perimeter's Claire™ to the Operating Room, a Landmark in Breast Cancer Surgery Using AI
news.summary: Intermountain Health became the first U.S. health system to commercially deploy Claire, now live at LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital under the systemwide agreement signed in January 2026. The release cites pivotal-trial margin accuracy of 88.1% and the roughly one-in-five lumpectomy patients who currently need a second operation; the shares jumped about 11% on the news.

news.headline: Perimeter Schedules Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call for August 20th
news.summary: Perimeter confirmed it will report Q2 2026 results after market close on Thursday, August 20, with a webcast and conference call at 5:00pm ET. The release also confirmed the final tranche of the LIFE offering - 1,955,500 units at C$0.35 on May 8, 2026 for C$684,425 - taking that offering to its C$7,521,150 maximum.

news.headline: Brookline starts Perimeter at buy; PT C$1.54
news.summary: Brookline Capital Markets analyst Kemp Doliver initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a C$1.54 target against a C$0.32 close on July 13, citing Claire's Breakthrough Device status as a tailwind for a CMS New Technology APC reimbursement decision he expects around year-end. The note models lumpectomy penetration well above 9% by 2035.

news.headline: Paradigm Capital names Perimeter and maintains Profound as healthcare Top Picks
news.summary: Paradigm Capital added Perimeter as a healthcare Top Pick with a Speculative Buy rating and a C$0.95 price target, with the stock at C$0.275 on July 3. The analyst frames the March 2026 FDA PMA approval of Claire as the accelerant for U.S. commercialization and flags M&A optionality versus comparable MedTech takeout multiples.

catalysts.label: Q2 2026 financial results
catalysts.detail: Perimeter reports Q2 2026 results after market close on August 20, with a call and webcast at 5:00pm ET. Watch for the first commentary on the Intermountain Health commercial launch, conversion out of the qualified-lead funnel, Claire pricing and recurring-revenue model, and the cash position after the roughly C$7.52M LIFE offering and C$6.04M convertible-debenture placement - Q1 closed with only about US$0.4M cash on hand against a ~US$3.0M quarterly net loss.

catalysts.label: Expansion of Claire across the Intermountain network
catalysts.detail: Claire is live at only two Intermountain sites (LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital) under a systemwide agreement. Roll-out to further Intermountain hospitals would be the cleanest near-term evidence that the first customer scales rather than stalls at a two-site pilot.

catalysts.label: Additional U.S. hospital system placements
catalysts.detail: With Intermountain live as the first commercial deployment, the market is watching for a second and third named U.S. health system to sign out of Perimeter's qualified-lead funnel. A second system would establish that the Intermountain deal is repeatable rather than a one-off flagship reference account.

catalysts.label: CMS New Technology APC / reimbursement decision
catalysts.detail: Management is pursuing a CMS New Technology APC pathway under the Medicare Outpatient Prospective Payment System for AI-enabled intraoperative OCT margin assessment, aided by Claire's Breakthrough Device Designation. Brookline's July note flags a decision expected by year-end 2026; this is a company/analyst expectation rather than a confirmed CMS date, and it is the single biggest driver of Claire's U.S. adoption economics.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results - first full quarter with Claire in commercial use
catalysts.detail: The Q3 print (typically reported in November) would be the first full reporting period after the August launch and the first chance to see actual Claire-related revenue and gross margin, versus a Q1 2026 base of roughly US$385K, all of it recurring revenue from the legacy S-Series installed base.

catalysts.label: Possible Nasdaq up-listing
catalysts.detail: Cited by sell-side analysts as a potential catalyst to broaden U.S. institutional access following FDA approval and commercial launch; the shares currently trade on the TSX Venture Exchange with an OTCQX quotation. No timeline has been announced and it would likely require a share consolidation and additional capital.

pulse: Perimeter has just delivered the proof point its whole 2026 thesis rested on: on August 13 Intermountain Health became the first U.S. health system to commercially deploy Claire, moving the only FDA PMA-approved AI-enabled breast-margin device from trials into live operating rooms at LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital, and the trade press (Medtech Insight, ITN) carried the story through the following week with encouraging first-user workflow feedback. The stock has roughly doubled off early-August levels near C$0.21 (about C$31M market cap) on that news, with Paradigm at C$0.95 and Brookline at C$1.54 on Buy-equivalent ratings. Everything now hinges on tonight's Q2 report: Q1 showed only ~US$385K of revenue, a ~US$3.0M quarterly net loss and about US$0.4M of cash before the spring raises (~C$7.52M LIFE offering plus ~C$6.04M of convertible debentures, part of it funded by the CEO), so the main risk is that a two-hospital launch and a still-pending CMS New Technology APC reimbursement decision leave the company needing more dilutive capital before Claire revenue is material.
